name: Dark Periwinkle
lede: Dark Periwinkle is a deep, saturated blue-violet, a shade down from [[periwinkle]] and classed by the ISCC-NBS system as a strong purplish blue.

sections.title: The name
sections.body:
The ISCC-NBS system of 1955 carries a block at this position, number 186, which covers several related moderate, pale, reddish, strong and light purplish blues [1]. The xkcd survey of 2010 later collected the plain descriptive phrase "dark periwinkle" from the public, and Wikipedia's own color list cites the ISCC-NBS block for its entry near this swatch [1].

No book in our library records who first drew the line at this exact depth of blue-violet, so its coinage as a named color stays undocumented here [1]. The nearest named colors on file are [[iris]], [[warm-blue]] and [[majorelle-blue]], at 2.9, 4.5 and 4.6 ΔE [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds no match for this exact swatch in its 23,781 paintings, using the standard CIEDE2000 and coverage test [2]. Saturated blue-violets of this depth are themselves rare in museum paint: many of the pigments that reach this chroma, such as synthetic ultramarine and some modern violets, postdate most of the archive or fade unevenly [2]. These are photographs of aged, varnished paintings, so an absence here says the shade is rare on surviving canvas, not that it was never mixed [2]. These are photographs of aged, varnished paintings, read as screen colors, not pigment identifications[2].
